title: Roman and neighboring polity boundaries
time_resolution: dated intervals rendered on an annual timeline
notes: Each geometry persists from FromYear through ToYear. Annual playback is display interpolation, not an annual observation. Geometry is simplified for web display.

title: Published and explicit Roman force estimates
time_resolution: seven irregular, non-interpolated estimates in four separately defined segments
notes: Only an ancient reported deployment, one explicit unit model, and published modern estimates remain. Lines connect points only when polity, scope, and estimation family are comparable. No western fifth-century total is plotted because the current evidence audit did not find a defensible published establishment estimate.

title: Reported and reconstructed rival campaign forces
time_resolution: dated campaign observations only
notes: Each row is one reported, reconstructed, or modern-minimum campaign force. The dataset deliberately contains no interpolated state-capacity series.

title: Republican Roman worked-metal comparison
time_resolution: third and second centuries BCE only
notes: Relative index with the nearest comparator normalized to 100. The public source supports the 25% comparison but not absolute kilograms for every army.

title: Physical and geographic basemap
time_resolution: not historical
notes: Modern coastlines, rivers, and borders provide orientation only and are not evidence for ancient political boundaries.

title: Roman and Western Han administrative scale and city-level governance
time_resolution: Western Han count at 5 BCE compared with an early-imperial Roman order-of-magnitude estimate
notes: Rome is normalized to 1 and Western Han to the published approximate ratio of 20. The Han count is recorded; the Roman ratio is a scholarly approximation. Governance descriptions are qualitative and do not convert local elites into imperial headcount.

title: Reconstructed Roman imperial budget scenarios
time_resolution: two snapshots, c. 150 and c. 215 CE, each with low and high scenarios
notes: Duncan-Jones's central-expenditure reconstruction as reproduced by Mattingly. Categories sum within each published scenario. Nominal totals across the two dates are not presented as real growth.

title: Roman fiscal rates, transfers, grain, and legionary pay
time_resolution: irregular dated observations from 123 BCE to 197 CE
notes: Each rate retains its own payer, base, geography, destination, and unit. The values are not combined into an empire-wide tax rate or a purchasing-power series.

title: Western Roman fiscal–military feedback evidence
time_resolution: seven selected mechanism anchors from 407 to 476 CE grouped by causal stage rather than plotted as a continuous chronology
notes: The rows expose the proposed chain from internal war through territorial and revenue loss to constrained recovery. They do not assign causal weights. The 445 assessment is local, the 58,000 figure is a fiscal equivalent, and 476 ends the western court only.

title: Selected western Roman fiscal-political shocks and recoveries
time_resolution: twelve selected dated events from 395 to 476 CE
notes: A selective chronology of interacting political, military, territorial, and fiscal changes. Event markers are not causal scores and do not imply a continuous decline.

title: Heather's African revenue-loss military equivalents
time_resolution: two regional components after the fifth-century African losses
notes: Published fiscal equivalents using Elton's annual maintenance costs. Values are not observed troop reductions or a western army census; the Proconsularis–Byzacena cavalry value is a lower bound.

title: Roman institutional afterlives on different clocks
time_resolution: irregular milestones from 312 BCE to 1453 CE plus three road-network summary measures
notes: Four parallel trajectories—roads, language, law, and the eastern Roman state—retain unlike evidence types and explicit limits. They are not combined into a legacy score.

title: Roman-road density and later outcomes in Europe and MENA
time_resolution: settlement around 500 CE and modern roads, night lights, and population
notes: Eight Table 5 coefficients and standard errors compare Europe with MENA under the paper's full controls. Coefficients are log-log elasticities, not physical survival shares or universal causal effects.

title: Administrative and lexical composition of the proto-cuneiform archive
time_resolution: Uruk IV and III phase summaries plus a corpus snapshot dated 19 May 2020
notes: Published bounded genre shares plus a retained CDLI corpus snapshot. The primary visual presents administrative shares as the complementary remainder of the lexical shares. Values describe surviving, cataloged material—not ancient production or a census of writing.

title: Uruk and comparative Mesopotamian settlement footprints
time_resolution: five irregular chronology intervals and six phase-level settlement-footprint observations from 4400 to 2900 BCE
notes: The primary visual compares published settlement footprints. Hectares are not converted into population; density and site-edge definitions vary; and the sparse Khirbet al-Fakhar scatter is not treated as equivalent to a dense city.

title: Natural channels and managed waterscapes around Uruk and southern Mesopotamia
time_resolution: irregular proxy and evidence intervals from 9700 to 1000 BCE plus one explicitly undated mixed-age palaeochannel layer
notes: The primary argument links a shifting freshwater ecology to long-lived human canals and urban concentration. Local borehole evidence, the Uruk-region canal interval, later dated canals, textual evidence, and the multi-period Eridu network remain distinct; the map is not a fourth-millennium time slice.

title: Cereal appropriability estimates and direct Uruk resource records
time_resolution: five qualitative resource comparisons, five claim-test observations, and two matched 952-society model estimates spanning direct Late Uruk evidence global comparative studies and an explicitly later Ur III methodological comparison
notes: The numeric fields reproduce matched 2SLS specifications from the published model's replication and its top-three-percent winsorization test; they are not a legibility score or local Uruk estimate. Direct Late Uruk records, regional deltaic ecology, and later evidence of archive bias remain separate, and archive visibility is not treated as dietary or economic share.

title: Archaeological routes into and out of early centralization
time_resolution: eight irregular site and regional observations from approximately 4200 to 3100 BCE
notes: Unlike observations retain their original units and inference limits. Counts are not added or converted into a fragility score; bowls do not establish slavery, walls do not measure coercion, abandonment is not a death count, and no Uruk disease series is inferred.

title: Urban scale, political centralization, and durable-notation evidence clocks across six regions
time_resolution: eighteen region-clock observations: seventeen phase ranges or dated contexts and one explicitly undated Andean notation gap
notes: The six-region frame is a debated comparative device, not a canonical list or rank. Urban scale, political centralization, and durable notation remain separate clocks. Dates are not annual series or confidence intervals; the Andean notation gap is not plotted at year zero.

title: Water rainfall crops transport and settlement-form profiles across six early urban regions
time_resolution: thirty region-dimension observations with source-specific places and phase or synthesis windows
notes: The six-by-five matrix computes no hydraulic, aridity, productivity, legibility, density, or state-causation score. Every cell preserves its evidence class and inference limit. Settlement form replaces a numeric density comparison because survey coverage, preservation, phase length, and population models are not commensurable.

title: Cities states notation monumental building and bronze evidence clocks across six regions
time_resolution: thirty region-milestone observations from 4000 BCE to 1521 CE including one explicitly undated Andean notation gap
notes: The existing city state and notation clocks are reused without changing their evidence status. Monument and bronze rows preserve regional thresholds: rare attestation sustained use analytical assemblage or regional scaling. Ordinal order is derived only from phase starts; bronze is not treated as a civilization score or prerequisite and the Andean notation gap is not plotted at year zero.

title: Institutional routes from resources and labor to coordinated action across six early urban regions
time_resolution: twenty-four unlike site phase regional and textual observations grouped as four inspectable routes per region
notes: Inputs coordinators and visible outcomes form qualitative evidence chains rather than measurements. Four rows per region are an editorial sampling frame not a prevalence count. The dataset computes no surplus tax storage labor coercion diversity or state-capacity score and every row preserves its inference limit.

title: Six regional pathways after early urban or political systems changed
time_resolution: six unlike site regional and political transition cases from the fourth millennium BCE to the first millennium CE
notes: Each row distinguishes a prior system an observable transition and a bounded afterlife. The cases are not synchronized and compute no collapse resilience continuity population-loss or civilizational score. Settlement persistence does not by itself establish population institutional or political continuity.

title: Copper and tin evidence places and connections across the Bronze Age Mediterranean and Eurasia
time_resolution: nineteen evidence-place rows and sixteen bounded connections from the eighteenth through thirteenth centuries BCE
notes: Four views keep one cargo Cypriot copper distribution Atlantic tin compatibility and a textual exchange relationship separate. Connections are evidence links not reconstructed routes. The dataset contains no annual trade volumes traffic estimates market shares or inferred direct voyages and preserves competing Uluburun tin-source claims.

title: Five selectively visible institutional circuits at Bronze Age palace centers
time_resolution: five unlike case windows from the early eighteenth through late thirteenth centuries BCE
notes: Each row follows one unusually visible resource or information circuit through an institutional aperture and keeps its outside-palace limit attached. Archive counts sheep tallies metal allotments and one silo episode retain unlike units and are never summed ranked or converted into a centralization or state-capacity score.

title: Five evidence windows onto Bronze Age chariot horses vehicles people upkeep and institutions
time_resolution: five unlike case windows from the fifteenth century BCE through the late Shang period
notes: The comparison preserves six dependencies without scoring completeness or effectiveness. Husiatyn lacks a vehicle; Kikkuli's at-least-184-day schedule is reconstructed; Pylian wheels are not complete chariots; EA 15 is a diplomatic gift; and Anyang mortuary contexts are not field organization.

title: Three shipwreck and two harbor windows onto plural Bronze Age maritime exchange
time_resolution: five unlike evidence windows and nineteen bounded associations from the seventeenth through twelfth centuries BCE
notes: Uluburun Cape Gelidonya Point Iria Kommos and Hala Sultan Tekke remain unlike cargo and harbor records. Connections identify material analytical or typological associations rather than direct voyages annual traffic market shares ownership or one unified trade institution.

title: Six unlike windows onto Late Bronze Age destruction contraction survival and reorganization
time_resolution: six non-synchronous windows from approximately 1250 to 1100 BCE including one explicitly comparative regional frame
notes: Environmental context conflict testimony institutional change and persistence remain prose evidence rather than additive variables. Date bands are orientation windows not annual measurements or uncertainty distributions. No shared collapse year cause score resilience score population loss or common attacker is inferred.

title: Five regional windows separating first iron evidence from wider adoption
time_resolution: five broad regional phase windows from the early second millennium through 500 BCE
notes: First evidence and wider adoption are separate synthesis windows. Five production dependencies remain prose evidence rather than scores. The dataset does not estimate annual output market share diffusion speed hardness fuel efficiency military power or a universal Iron Age threshold.

title: Eleven measured modern bloomery experiments from Meroe and Sehnde reconstruction programs
time_resolution: individual modern experimental runs rather than a historical time series
notes: Ore charcoal and reported bloom masses stay at run level. Charcoal per kilogram of bloom is a transparent derived ratio. Zero and trace outputs remain categories; the data do not estimate ancient output woodland loss labor weapon totals or civilization-level efficiency.

title: Paired bloom and forged-bar metallography from four controlled smelting experiments
time_resolution: eight samples from four modern experimental runs rather than a historical series
notes: Hardness means sample counts standard deviations chemistry microstructure and forgeability remain distinct. The dataset does not convert hardness into toughness weapon performance service life battlefield effect or a material-superiority score.

title: Four bounded cases separating equipment access from recruitment supply and replacement
time_resolution: one Bronze Age campaign structure one broad pre-Roman transition and two same-model Punic War strategic maxima
notes: Only the Carthaginian and Roman values share a model family and receive proportional bars. Kadesh remains a campaign inference and the pre-Roman civitas case has no headcount. The dataset contains no kilograms per soldier artifact-derived army total replacement curve causal share or military-power score.

title: Five bounded iron-production architectures from household networks to royal and state systems
time_resolution: five unlike institutional cases from the ninth century BCE through the fifth century CE
notes: Inputs making coordination distribution and visible evidence remain separate. The rows do not calculate output centralization market integration state capacity productivity labor totals or a universal development sequence.

title: Herodotus's Sardis–Susa itinerary and four bounded road-and-relay evidence classes
time_resolution: six itinerary segments and four source-bounded evidence windows from 509 to 480 BCE and mid-fifth-century reporting
notes: The itinerary preserves stages and parasangs without kilometre conversion. Ninety days is Herodotus's arithmetic; the relay description has no end-to-end duration; the Persepolis archive is regional. No imperial-speed score route geometry traffic estimate or universal travel model is produced.

title: Five source-bounded Achaemenid provincial governance portfolios
time_resolution: five unlike administrative windows between 522 and 334 BCE rather than a continuous provincial series
notes: Top office local partners obligations royal connection visible action and inference limit remain separate. The dataset does not treat tribute districts as identical to satrapies or calculate autonomy centralization loyalty tax control population revenue or a universal provincial hierarchy.

title: Herodotus's twenty tribute districts and seven source-bounded obligation portfolios
time_resolution: twenty reported districts and seven unlike evidence windows from the early fifth through mid-fifth century BCE
notes: Only the nineteen silver district rows share an internal Herodotean scale. Indian gold dust horses grain people services gifts cuneiform assessments and Apadana imagery remain unlike evidence. No modern value per-capita burden tax rate effective incidence or empire-wide revenue total is inferred.

title: Six source-bounded windows on Achaemenid military assembly, command, support, and coordination
time_resolution: six unlike windows between 509 and 331 BCE rather than a continuous force series
notes: Contributor labels command links battlefield functions supply evidence and coordination tests remain separate. Ancient headline army and fleet totals are excluded, and the dataset does not infer ethnic shares equipment ranks combat power or exact army composition.

title: Eighteen source-bounded episodes across five Achaemenid institutional afterlife pathways
time_resolution: eighteen unlike episodes from 550 BCE to 651 CE grouped into five pathways rather than a continuous institutional index
notes: Provincial retention military experiment script descent local recombination and royal-title revival remain distinct relationships. Bar length marks evidence dates only; the dataset does not calculate continuity influence centralization Persianization state capacity institutional strength or importance.

title: Five mobilizing capacities and six final Qin conquest endpoints
time_resolution: five unlike institutional windows from 453 to 208 BCE and six political endpoints from 230 to 221 BCE
notes: The capacities form a causal synthesis rather than five dated inventions. Qin is the best-documented winner rather than the only reforming state. Conquest dates mark courts rather than annual boundaries; no army total casualty count population series territory series combat-power estimate or state-capacity score is inferred.

title: Six Qin norm-to-practice windows across measures, script, tablets, and grain tallies
time_resolution: six unlike windows centered on 222 to 208 BCE with the script critique extending across a longer epigraphic chronology
notes: Four row-specific bounded counts use twenty-five Qianling reports or twenty-two grain tallies; they are not averaged. Certification does not prove replacement, official script does not imply spoken-language unity, and no empire-wide compliance literacy efficiency loyalty or state-capacity score is inferred.

title: Eight source-bounded Qin and Han logistics windows from production through maintenance
time_resolution: eight unlike windows from the late fourth century BCE through 25 CE rather than an annual infrastructure or throughput series
notes: Production storage transport maintenance and labor extraction remain separate. The Western Han Capital Granary is not back-projected into Qin and the dataset calculates no annual grain flow irrigated area wall length labor total household burden megaproject workforce or state-capacity score.

title: Six changes in the Han center-kingdom bargain
time_resolution: six dated windows from 202 to 106 BCE
notes: Direct-commandery counts are three published anchors, not area shares or a centralization index.

title: Six steps from late-Han emergency response to rival states
time_resolution: six dated windows from 184 to 229 CE
notes: The sequence presents a mechanism, not a single-cause model; army, rebel, and casualty totals are excluded.

title: Published territorial-growth anchors for Achaemenid Persia, Western Han, and Rome
time_resolution: twenty-five sparse published anchors reset to the first selected estimate for each polity
notes: Lines between anchors are visual interpolation, not annual observations. Western Han begins at inherited Qin scale; the comparison does not treat frontier control as equally intensive or splice Cliopatria map areas into the Taagepera series.

title: Twenty-four published Indus weight-series means and four monumental-ruler evidence categories
time_resolution: three excavation series grouped into eight common weight ratios and four century-scale archaeological absence categories
notes: Published means and sample sizes remain series-specific. Implied units are exact mean divided by ratio. No political-centralization score, ruler count, market volume, bulk-goods flow, social-equality score, or claim that rulers were absent is inferred.

title: Four source-bounded windows in the Begash pastoral and horse sequence
time_resolution: four broad windows from the third to first millennia BCE at one south-eastern Kazakhstan settlement
notes: Faunal fragment shares are not herd population diet wealth cavalry or pan-steppe adoption rates.

title: Seven generally accepted Pauline letters in rough chronological order
time_resolution: seven approximate dates from 51 to 57 CE
notes: Surviving letters are not a census of Christians congregations travel or transmission; Philemon has no securely assigned destination here.

title: Six broad regional incorporation windows from Arabia to Transoxiana
time_resolution: six endpoints or intervals from 632 to 751 CE rather than annual boundaries
notes: Broad political incorporation does not mean uniform control conversion cultural unity or demographic replacement.

title: Cumulative territory categories among 636 approximately classified poleis
time_resolution: one bounded distribution assembled from Archaic and Classical poleis rather than annual boundaries
notes: Cumulative approximate categories are not simultaneous borders; territory is not population wealth military power democracy or independence.

title: Selected named contingents in Polybius's order of battle at Raphia
time_resolution: one battle in 217 BCE
notes: Ancient transmitted figures are not audited payrolls. The Egyptian/phalanx textual ambiguity is preserved and no new army total or ethnic share is calculated.

title: Three documented forms of money at the Turfan oasis
time_resolution: documentary evidence spanning 273 to 796 CE
notes: Coexistence does not measure market shares total trade values or use across every Silk Road economy.

title: Modeled Western European manuscript production by century
time_resolution: ten century totals from the sixth through fifteenth centuries
notes: Estimated copies produced are corrected from surviving manuscripts and are not surviving-book counts readership literacy or annual observations.

title: Reported Ghanaian trade dues and gold-nugget rule in al-Bakri
time_resolution: one eleventh-century written account of reported rules
notes: Reported dues are not observed receipts or volumes. Dinars mithqals goods and the nugget rule are kept unlike and unsummed.

title: Five archaeological industry lenses at Khao Sam Kaeo
time_resolution: one port settlement broadly dated to the fourth through second centuries BCE
notes: Industry categories show local production evidence and technological analogies rather than comparable output workforce or artisan ethnicity.

title: Five published measures from the PACUNAM lidar survey
time_resolution: one 2016 survey and a modeled Late Classic regional peak
notes: The mapped survey footprint and structures are direct lidar results; population density and total population are regional models with different scope.

title: Five unlike measures of the Qhapaq Ñan
time_resolution: multi-century network at its fifteenth-century maximum plus a modern selected heritage property
notes: Network length route count topographic reach imperial extent and the inscribed sample retain different scopes and are not combined.

title: Historical and genomic evidence for a Central Eurasian plague source
time_resolution: one 1338–1339 epidemic context compared with published plague genomes
notes: Sample counts detections reconstructed genomes and phylogenetic placement are unlike observations. The study does not establish a transmission route or political cause.

title: Published European military scale and cost multipliers
time_resolution: four published multipliers and one normalized comparison baseline
notes: Army and annual war-cost multipliers use different measures and baselines and are never combined.

title: Manila Galleon chronology monopoly rule and voyage failure shares
time_resolution: route chronology plus sample-wide descriptive shares across 1565–1815
notes: Failure includes shipwreck or a heavily damaged return to port; subgroup shares are not causal estimates.

title: Building-laborer subsistence ratios in London Amsterdam and Beijing
time_resolution: two half-century averages per city from 1700 through 1799
notes: Ratios depend on a bare-bones family basket and full-employment assumptions and are not citywide or national median incomes.

title: Regional Indus crop calendars at Harappa Khirsara and Masudpur VII
time_resolution: site-specific phase sequences rather than synchronized annual observations
notes: Exact assemblage shares are preserved only where published. Qualitative crop presence is not converted into acreage output yield or diet.

title: Urban fabric and political order across three Early Historic South Asian phases
time_resolution: three broad and regionally asynchronous phases from 600 BCE through 300 CE
notes: Named sites polities and material features are illustrative examples rather than a complete census or one urbanization score.

title: Four inscriptional windows onto Mauryan regional rule
time_resolution: selected third-century-BCE royal prescriptions and named administrative relationships
notes: Edict locations, inspection schedules, regional centers, and named neighbors are not combined into a boundary, control score, or measure of compliance.

title: Three material and literary networks beyond South Asian political rule
time_resolution: three asynchronous case windows from the fourth century BCE through the fifth century CE onward
notes: Unlike workshop commodity and language evidence is compared without creating one diffusion score political boundary or continuous cultural zone.

title: Four evidence windows from local horse husbandry to mounted cavalry
time_resolution: four asynchronous windows from the fourth millennium BCE through the mid-first millennium BCE
notes: Genomes graves and surviving tack identify different capabilities and are not converted into one adoption date travel speed action radius or military-power score.

title: Three textual windows from recurring contributions to rules and named distribution roles
time_resolution: three asynchronous textual windows from about 54 to 155 CE
notes: Prescriptions and an apologetic account show institutional mechanisms but are not audited budgets observed compliance a congregation census or a measured survival rate.

title: Four evidence windows from inherited fiscal machinery to caliphal standardization
time_resolution: four asynchronous windows from 643 through 703 CE
notes: A papyrus regional administrative syntheses coin types and dated reforms answer different questions and are not one tax rate language share staff count or empire-wide switch date.
